instructions: Peel the cucumbers fully. Halve them lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and slice them thin on an angle.
Toss the slices with 1 1/2 tsp of the salt in a bowl and leave them for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, put the rice and 2 1/4 cups of water in a pot over high heat. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Beat the eggs with 1/4 tsp salt in a bowl and set them aside. Mince the garlic.
Rinse the cucumber slices under cold water, drain them and pat them dry with paper towels.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir for a few seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the cucumbers and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until they're hot all the way through and no longer raw tasting.
Push the cucumbers to one side. Pour the eggs onto the empty side and leave them for 20 seconds, until the bottom sets.
Stir the eggs into big soft curds and toss them with the cucumbers. Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look a little wet.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt, then crack the pepper over the top.
method_notes: Lead is Delightful Plate (4.58 from 19, so just under the 20 rating mark and a fallback). It salts and rinses the cucumber, then stir-fries it for 1 to 2 minutes with garlic and folds in the eggs last. Cooking with Lei cooks the eggs first and braises the cucumber with a cornstarch sauce; Omnivore's Cookbook adds soy and sesame. The soy and sesame oil are left out to keep it gluten-free. Amounts are doubled from the source's 2 servings. Rice is added so the timeline includes it.
